prompt: A national coffee chain is deciding whether to open cafés in airports. The candidate's framework: (1) Airport traveler demand and spending; (2) Competition from existing airport food outlets; (3) Lease and operating costs at airports; (4) Rent and revenue-sharing terms with the airport. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.feedback: Right. Both buckets cover what the airport charges. Merge them and use the space for whether the chain can operate in airports.

options.text: Missing: whether the brand appeals to travelers
options.feedback: Brand appeal sits inside traveler demand (bucket 1). The flaw is that buckets 3 and 4 both cover airport charges.

options.text: Bucket 2 doesn't matter, since travelers have few options
options.feedback: Competing outlets decide how much of the traffic the chain can win, so bucket 2 matters.

options.text: It is a generic profit tree rather than airport-specific
options.feedback: Every bucket is specific to airports. The flaw is the overlap between buckets 3 and 4.

explanation: Buckets 3 and 4 both describe what the airport charges. A MECE version: traveler demand, competition, airport economics (lease, revenue share, staffing), and the chain's ability to operate in airports.

extras.corrected_framework: Traveler demand; competition; airport economics (lease, revenue share, staffing); ability to operate in airports
